y-m-11-09.title: Wetin day of week e go be in 50 days?
y-m-11-09.s.s2.prompt: Wetin day of week e go be in 50 days?
y-m-11-09.topic: Finding day of week after some days with repeating rule (day-of-week cycle)
y-m-11-09.goal: Use rule say same weekday return every 7 days to find weekday after some days, find and correct mistake of treating 50 as same weekday as 49 because dem look similar, then make several day-counts wey fit conditions.
y-m-11-09.material: Today na Thursday. Weekdays continue going around in order Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Jiho wan find, "Wetin day of week e go be in 50 days?" Read Jiho solution.
y-m-11-09.thinking.0: Finding wrong generalization in repeating pattern
y-m-11-09.thinking.2: Making several day-counts wey fit conditions
y-m-11-09.prereq.0: Weekday order and counting 'some days later', one week na 7 days (Grade 3–4 level)
y-m-11-09.s.s1.prompt: Choose line for Jiho solution wey hard to believe.
y-m-11-09.s.s1.hint.0: For each line, write how many days later di 'same day of week return' really be.
y-m-11-09.s.s1.hint.1: Check whether weekday 49 days later and 50 days later na the same or different by counting on one day at a time.
y-m-11-09.s.s1.line.0: After 7 days, same day of week return. After 7 days na Thursday.
y-m-11-09.s.s1.line.1: After 14 days and 21 days, Thursday too.
y-m-11-09.s.s1.line.2: After 49 days na Thursday too. 50 close to 49, so after 50 days e go Thursday too.
y-m-11-09.s.s1.explain: Line 3 na problem. Statement say 49 days later Thursday correct. But 50 no be 49, so you no fit say e be same weekday. Numbers looking similar no be evidence say weekday same. Line 4 conclusion trust line 3, so e wrong too. We go find weekday for 50 days in next question.
y-m-11-09.s.s2.hint.0: Among day counts wey bring same weekday again, find one closest to 50.
y-m-11-09.s.s2.hint.1: From weekday after that number of days, continue counting for remaining days.
y-m-11-09.s.s2.r.a: You treat 50 days as same weekday as 49 days later. Think wetin happen when one more day pass after 49 days.
y-m-11-09.s.s2.r.b: Dis na idea of adding leftover days after weekday returns to weekday itself.
y-m-11-09.s.s2.r.c: Dis na idea of taking leftover days as 2 days. Count how many days apart 49 days later and 50 days later be.
y-m-11-09.s.s2.r.d: Dis na idea of counting one day backward from 49 days later. Think whether 50 days later earlier or later than 49.
y-m-11-09.s.s2.explain: 49 days later na Thursday, and 50 days later na di next day, so e Friday. You fit read am as 7 days seven times make 49 days, with one day remaining.
y-m-11-09.s.s3.prompt: When today na Thursday, make 3 different number of days later wey e go be Saturday. (Number of days d na natural number from 1 to 60.)
y-m-11-09.s.s3.hint.0: When today na Thursday, write weekdays for 1 day later, 2 days later, 3 days later in order, and find number of days when e first become Saturday.
y-m-11-09.s.s3.hint.1: Also check weekdays for numbers you get by adding 7 days each time to dat number.
y-m-11-09.s.s3.ok.c1: E be number of days from 1 to 60.
y-m-11-09.s.s3.fail.c1: Make number of days natural number from 1 to 60.
y-m-11-09.s.s3.ok.c2: After dis number of days, na Saturday.
y-m-11-09.s.s3.fail.c2: After dis number of days, no be Saturday. Think how many days e take from Thursday reach Saturday, and wetin happen when one week pass.
y-m-11-09.s.s3.explain: 2 days after Thursday na Saturday. Same weekday return every 7 days, so 9 days, 16 days, 23 days, … Saturday too. Inside 60 days, 2, 9, 16, 23, 30, 37, 44, 51, 58 days later na Saturday.

y-m-11-06.title: Ways to share 24 sweets into bags
y-m-11-06.topic: Di connection between number of bags and number for each bag (when total stay di same)
y-m-11-06.goal: Find relationship for table about how number for each bag change as number of bags increase. Make several ways wey fit conditions and judge say some cases no possible.
y-m-11-06.material:
You wan share 24 sweets into bags with same number for each one. You put all sweets, none remain. Look di table.
When number of bags na 2, each bag get 12; when bags na 3, each get 8; when bags na 4, each get 6.
y-m-11-06.thinking.0: Pick di relationship wey correct for table (remove relationships wey correct only for some cells)
y-m-11-06.thinking.1: Make several ways under one condition
y-m-11-06.prereq.0: Know numbers for multiplication table (Grade 2–3 level)
y-m-11-06.prereq.1: Read how 2 quantities change in table
y-m-11-06.s.s1.prompt: Look di table and choose di best statement about relationship between number of bags and number of sweets in each bag.
y-m-11-06.s.s1.hint.0: For each of di 3 cells, write sum, difference, and multiple of di 2 numbers.
y-m-11-06.s.s1.hint.1: Find di one wey give same value for all 3 cells.
y-m-11-06.s.s1.o.a: Each time number of bags increase by 1, sweets in each bag decrease by 4.
y-m-11-06.s.s1.r.a: You only look first 2 cells (12→8). Check whether e also decrease by 4 in third cell (8→6).
y-m-11-06.s.s1.o.b: If you add number of bags and number of sweets in one bag, you always get same number.
y-m-11-06.s.s1.r.b: If you add di 2 numbers in each cell, you get 14, 11, 10. Check cell by cell whether di sums same.
y-m-11-06.s.s1.o.c: If you multiply number of bags by number of sweets in each bag, you always get 24.
y-m-11-06.s.s1.r.c: Dis choice check whether value wey come from di 2 numbers stay di same for 3 cells.
y-m-11-06.s.s1.o.d: Number of sweets in one bag na 6 times number of bags.
y-m-11-06.s.s1.r.d: Na 6 times only for first cell (2→12). For second cell, check whether 6 times di number of bags, 3, equal 8.
y-m-11-06.s.s1.explain: For all 3 cells, product na 24: 2×12=24, 3×8=24, 4×6=24. Na because all 24 sweets dey inside. Di sums and di numbers wey decrease differ for each cell.
y-m-11-06.s.s2.prompt: Find cases wey no dey for table. Make 2 different ways to put all 24 sweets in with nothing left. Number of bags a na 5 or more, and each bag must hold b sweets, wey na 2 or more.
y-m-11-06.s.s2.hint.0: Like di 3 cells of table, choose number of bags one by one and find how many must dey in each bag to make 24.
y-m-11-06.s.s2.hint.1: Keep only cells where number of bags na 5 or more and each bag get 2 or more.
y-m-11-06.s.s2.var.b: Number of sweets in one bag
y-m-11-06.s.s2.ok.c1: Number of bags na natural number wey be 5 or more, and number of sweets in one bag na natural number wey be 2 or more.
y-m-11-06.s.s2.fail.c1: Make number of bags 5 or more, and number of sweets in each bag a natural number wey be 2 or more.
y-m-11-06.s.s2.fail.c2: Di total wey come from number of bags and sweets in each bag no be 24. Check di relationship wey you find for table.
y-m-11-06.s.s2.explain: Ways wey fit di conditions na 6 bags with 4 sweets each, 8 bags with 3 each, and 12 bags with 2 each. 4 bags with 6 each get less than 5 bags, and 24 bags with 1 each no meet condition say each bag must get 2 or more. (Ways wey only switch di numbers, like 6 bags with 4 each and 4 bags with 6 each, count as different ways.)
y-m-11-06.s.s3.prompt: When you get 5 bags, you fit put all 24 sweets with same number in each bag and no sweet remain?
y-m-11-06.s.s3.hint.0: Change number for each bag to 1, 2, 3, … and write total for 5 bags.
y-m-11-06.s.s3.hint.1: Check whether any total match 24, or whether di number jump pass 24.
y-m-11-06.s.s3.o.a: You no fit put same number in each bag and get nothing remain.
y-m-11-06.s.s3.r.a: Dis judgment come from checking cases where both number of bags and number in each bag na natural numbers.
y-m-11-06.s.s3.r.b: 5 bags with 4 each na 20. Check whether all 24 sweets don enter.
y-m-11-06.s.s3.r.c: 5 bags with 5 each na 25. Check whether na 24 sweets.
y-m-11-06.s.s3.o.d: E depend on how many go each bag, so I no fit tell.
y-m-11-06.s.s3.r.d: You no try possible numbers one by one. Change di number to 1, 2, 3, … and write di total.
y-m-11-06.s.s3.explain: If you put 4 in each of 5 bags, na 20; if you put 5, na 25, so neither one match 24 exactly. If you divide 24 evenly into 5 bags, e no divide into whole natural number, so e impossible.

y-m-11-01.title: Wetin number come after 2, 4, 8?
y-m-11-01.topic: Rules for number patterns: decide whether same beginning must give only one next number
y-m-11-01.goal: Understand say first few numbers of pattern fit no fix only one rule. Make next numbers using different rules, and talk wetin else you need.
y-m-11-01.material: Jihu arrange number cards in row. Di first 3 na 2, 4, 8. Jihu talk, “Di next card definitely na 16!” All numbers for di cards na natural numbers, and one rule decide di next number from di number before am.
y-m-11-01.thinking.0: Check whether di claim really “definitely” true
y-m-11-01.thinking.1: Make your own different rule wey explain di same data
y-m-11-01.thinking.2: Judge whether information enough and talk wetin more you need
y-m-11-01.prereq.0: Check difference and multiple between neighbor numbers in number pattern (Grade 3–4 level)
y-m-11-01.prereq.1: Basics of calculating with natural numbers
y-m-11-01.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you think about Jihu words, “Di next card definitely na 16”?
y-m-11-01.s.s1.hint.0: Write side by side wetin change and how, going from 2 to 4 and from 4 to 8.
y-m-11-01.s.s1.hint.1: Apart from checking “how many times,” also write “how much dem add,” then compare both ways.
y-m-11-01.s.s1.o.a: 16 correct. Because 2, 4, 8 grow by doubling di number before.
y-m-11-01.s.s1.r.a: E true say 2, 4, 8 follow di doubling rule. But you never check whether another rule fit give di same 3 numbers.
y-m-11-01.s.s1.o.b: You fit know whether e be 16 only after checking whether another rule fit give 2, 4, 8.
y-m-11-01.s.s1.r.b: Dis idea no stop after finding one rule; e check whether another rule fit make di same number pattern.
y-m-11-01.s.s1.o.c: Di numbers dey get bigger, so di next card fit be any number bigger than 8.
y-m-11-01.s.s1.r.c: You only use di fact say e dey get bigger, and no check how much bigger each time. How about checking di relationship between neighboring numbers?
y-m-11-01.s.s1.o.d: Only 3 cards dey, so we no fit say one rule dey or know di next number.
y-m-11-01.s.s1.r.d: You no use di condition “one rule dey.” If one rule dey, you fit look for possible rules from di 3 cards.
y-m-11-01.s.s1.explain: You fit get 2, 4, 8 from rule “double di number before,” and also from rule “di number wey dem add to di number before increase by 2, like 2, 4.” Di next number depend on di rule, so e hard to say na 16 from only 3 cards.
y-m-11-01.s.s2.prompt: Make we test wetin Jihu talk. Make 2 different numbers wey fit come after 2, 4, 8. Di next number must follow one of these rules: (가) each time multiply di number before by some number, or (나) di number wey dem add to di number before increase by di same amount each time.
y-m-11-01.s.s2.hint.0: First find “how many times” and “how much dem add” going from 2 to 4 and from 4 to 8.
y-m-11-01.s.s2.hint.1: Write di number you get if you apply each rule to 8 one more time.
y-m-11-01.s.s2.ok.c1: Di next number na natural number bigger than 8.
y-m-11-01.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg make di next number natural number bigger than 8.
y-m-11-01.s.s2.ok.c2: E na number wey follow one of di 2 rules.
y-m-11-01.s.s2.fail.c2: Dis number no come after 2, 4, 8 according to rule (가) or rule (나). Apply both rules one time to 8.
y-m-11-01.s.s2.explain: With rule (가), doubling, e be 16, na 8 doubled. With rule (나), where di added number increase by 2 as 2, 4, 6, e be 8+6=14. Di same first 3 numbers fit have different next number.
y-m-11-01.s.s3.prompt: Jihu explain di rule with words: “Di number wey dem add to di number before increase by 2 each time.” According to dis rule, wetin be di number on di card after 2, 4, 8?
y-m-11-01.s.s3.hint.0: Follow di rule dem tell you, first write di numbers dem add for 2→4 and 4→8.
y-m-11-01.s.s3.hint.1: Next, write how di added number change and add am to 8.
y-m-11-01.s.s3.r.a: You still dey use rule of continuing by doubling di number before. Di rule dem just tell you na about di added number.
y-m-11-01.s.s3.r.b: You keep di added number as 4. For di rule wey dem tell you, di added number change each time.
y-m-11-01.s.s3.r.c: Dis idea continue di added numbers as 2, 4, 6.
y-m-11-01.s.s3.r.d: You add 2 to 8. Continue di flow where di added number grow from 2 to 4.
y-m-11-01.s.s3.explain: When dem give di rule with words, di next number become only one. Di added numbers na 2, 4, 6, so 8+6=14. When dem only give few numbers, di next number fit no be only one; dem fix am if dem tell you di rule or one more next number.

y-m-11-07.prereq.1: Basics of calculating with natural numbers
y-m-11-07.prereq.0: Reading how two quantities change together in table (Grade 3–4 level)
y-m-11-07.title: Minseo and her big sister ages, explaining to younger cousin
y-m-11-07.topic: Explain relationship wey add fixed amount, like age gap, with words and examples
y-m-11-07.goal: Find relationship for table where fixed difference stay di same, like ages. Find values, then rewrite di relationship with words and examples wey Grade 2 cousin fit understand.
y-m-11-07.material: Minseo and her big sister count their ages from di day dem born in di same year (each year both grow one year). When Minseo 4, her sister 7; when Minseo 5, her sister 8; and when Minseo 6, her sister 9. Minseo wan tell her cousin, wey dey Grade 2, how dem decide her sister age.
y-m-11-07.thinking.0: Find di relationship (difference stay same) for table and predict new value
y-m-11-07.thinking.1: Change explanation to fit who dey listen
y-m-11-07.thinking.2: Use example check whether explanation correct
y-m-11-07.s.s1.prompt: When Minseo turn 10, how old her sister go be?
y-m-11-07.s.s1.hint.0: For each of di 3 cells, find di difference between sister age and Minseo age.
y-m-11-07.s.s1.hint.1: Check whether di difference same or different in each cell, and compare how many years each person grow every year.
y-m-11-07.s.s1.r.a: You add sister first age, 7, to Minseo age 10. Check whether method correct by using table where sister 7 when Minseo 4.
y-m-11-07.s.s1.r.b: You take am say na 2 times Minseo age. Check whether 2 times correct for cells where age 5 and 6 dey for table.
y-m-11-07.s.s1.r.c: You take di age gap between Minseo and her sister as 4. Find difference between both ages in one table cell.
y-m-11-07.s.s1.r.d: Dis idea use fact say both ages increase by same amount each year.
y-m-11-07.s.s1.explain: For all 3 cells, sister dey 3 years older than Minseo (7-4=3, 8-5=3, 9-6=3). Each year both grow one year, so di difference no change. So when Minseo 10, her sister go be 13.
y-m-11-07.s.s2.prompt: Choose di best explanation for Minseo to send her cousin (Grade 2).
y-m-11-07.s.s2.hint.0: First check whether each explanation fit all 3 table cells.
y-m-11-07.s.s2.hint.1: Among explanations with correct relationship, choose di one Grade 2 cousin fit follow.
y-m-11-07.s.s2.o.a: My sister age na “Minseo age + 3.” You find am by adding 3 to my age, you get am?
y-m-11-07.s.s2.r.a: Di equation correct, but cousin wey no sabi symbols or equations may need words and example first.
y-m-11-07.s.s2.o.b: My sister about 2 times my age. When I 4, my sister 7.
y-m-11-07.s.s2.r.b: You describe relationship from values wey look similar for one cell. Check for table how old my sister when I 6.
y-m-11-07.s.s2.o.c: My sister always 3 years older than me. When I 8, my sister 11.
y-m-11-07.s.s2.r.c: You explain relationship with words and example wey easy for di listener to follow.
y-m-11-07.s.s2.o.d: My sister age always na 7, even when my age change.
y-m-11-07.s.s2.r.d: You say e no change after looking only at value for first cell. Check for table my sister age when I 5.
y-m-11-07.s.s2.explain: c talk correct relationship in short words (always 3 years older) and example, so Grade 2 cousin fit follow. a also correct, but e fit hard for cousin wey no used to equations to understand from di start. b and d no be correct relationship.
y-m-11-07.s.s2.acc.0: Di relationship correct. For Grade 2 cousin, e go even better if you add words and an example.
y-m-11-07.s.s3.prompt: Now become Minseo and write explanation to send your cousin. Talk how dem decide sister age, and also say how old sister go be when Minseo 20.
y-m-11-07.s.s3.hint.0: Use one cell for table as example, first write one sentence saying how many years older sister be.
y-m-11-07.s.s3.hint.1: Write how to find di age 20 one step at a time so your cousin fit follow.
y-m-11-07.s.s3.placeholder: Example: My sister dey ... years older than me
y-m-11-07.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You write di relationship with easy words your cousin fit understand?
y-m-11-07.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You give example wey your cousin fit try follow by themselves?
y-m-11-07.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You put your explanation into other table cells to check say e correct?
y-m-11-07.s.s3.model.0: My sister always dey 3 years older than me. When I 5, my sister 8. So when I turn 20, my sister go be 20 plus 3, wey na 23 years old.
y-m-11-07.s.s3.model.1: Di age gap between us always na 3 years. When I 4, my sister 7; when I turn 20, na 20+3=23, so my sister go be 23.
y-m-11-07.s.s3.modelNote.1: An explanation wey write equation only once

y-m-11-02.title: Looking at Minsu equation for di apple box table
y-m-11-02.topic: Read how 2 quantities match in table and write am as equation (relationship wey increase by di same number)
y-m-11-02.goal: Test equation wey correct in only one table cell against all cells, correct am, then write di same relationship as equations in 2 directions.
y-m-11-02.material:
Fruit shop dey sell apples in boxes. Each box hold di same number of apples. Minsu arrange di number of boxes and apples in table.
When number of boxes na 1, apples na 5; when boxes na 2, apples na 10; when boxes na 3, apples na 15.
Minsu talk, “If you add 4 to number of boxes, you get number of apples.”
y-m-11-02.thinking.0: Find mistake in general rule wey correct in only one cell
y-m-11-02.thinking.1: Check equation using several cells of di table
y-m-11-02.thinking.2: Write di same relationship as different equation
y-m-11-02.prereq.0: Read table of 2 quantities wey change together (Grade 3–4 level)
y-m-11-02.prereq.1: Basics of calculating with natural numbers (Grade 3 level)
y-m-11-02.s.s1.prompt: Follow Minsu thinking. Which line hard to believe? Choose one.
y-m-11-02.s.s1.hint.0: For each line, separate lines wey copy table numbers as dem be from lines wey draw new conclusion.
y-m-11-02.s.s1.hint.1: Put di equation from di line wey draw new conclusion into other table cells and compare am with di table values.
y-m-11-02.s.s1.line.0: If 1 box dey, 5 apples dey, and 1 plus 4 na 5.
y-m-11-02.s.s1.line.2: So I think adding 4 to number of boxes always give number of apples.
y-m-11-02.s.s1.line.3: If you use dis equation for 3 boxes, 3 plus 4 give 7 apples.
y-m-11-02.s.s1.explain: Line 3 na di problem. Dem check am only in first table cell (1 box), then talk say “always.” So line 4 give 7, but di table say 15 when 3 boxes dey. Lines 1 and 2 copy di table, so dem okay. Correct for one cell no mean correct for every cell.
y-m-11-02.s.s2.prompt: Choose all relationships wey correct for all 3 cells of di table.
y-m-11-02.s.s2.hint.0: Put numbers from first, second, and third table cells into each equation one by one.
y-m-11-02.s.s2.hint.1: First cross out equations wey no correct for even one of di 3 cells.
y-m-11-02.s.s2.o.a: Number of boxes + 5 = number of apples
y-m-11-02.s.s2.r.a: 1+5=6, wey different from 5 apples even for first cell.
y-m-11-02.s.s2.o.b: Number of boxes × 5 = number of apples
y-m-11-02.s.s2.r.b: Dis choice check di 3 table cells using relationship of multiplying number of boxes by 5.
y-m-11-02.s.s2.o.c: Number of boxes × 2 + 3 = number of apples
y-m-11-02.s.s2.r.c: E correct for first cell, but check for second cell (2 boxes).
y-m-11-02.s.s2.o.d: Number of apples ÷ 5 = number of boxes
y-m-11-02.s.s2.r.d: You read same relationship backward too, finding box number from apple number.
y-m-11-02.s.s2.o.e: Number of apples − number of boxes = 4
y-m-11-02.s.s2.r.e: Na 4 only for first cell. Find di difference for second cell.
y-m-11-02.s.s2.explain: If you multiply box number by 5, you get apple number (1×5=5, 2×5=10, 3×5=15), and if you divide apple number by 5, you get box number. Both equations talk same relationship forward and backward. Other equations correct only for one or two cells.
y-m-11-02.s.s3.prompt: Minsu wan correct im first equation. Write how e go be good to correct am and how you go check whether equation correct.
y-m-11-02.s.s3.hint.0: Put number from second cell of table inside equation wey you make now.
y-m-11-02.s.s3.hint.1: First write equation in words. 'When one more box dey, how many more apples dey?'
y-m-11-02.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You put numbers yourself check say corrected equation correct in other table cells too, no be only first one?
y-m-11-02.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You explain relationship between number of boxes and number of apples with words 'so many each'?
y-m-11-02.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You realize say you fit also talk am with another equation?
y-m-11-02.s.s3.model.0: Correct am to equation wey multiply box number by 5 (number of boxes × 5 = number of apples). I check say all three table cells correct: 1×5=5, 2×5=10, 3×5=15.
y-m-11-02.s.s3.model.1: Each box get 5, so apple number dey increase by 5, as 5, 10, 15. So I write number of apples ÷ 5 = number of boxes, and I fit check say 15÷5=3 correctly give 3 boxes.
y-m-11-02.s.s3.modelNote.1: Answer wey write division equation and check at least one cell

y-m-11-03.prereq.0: Read table of 2 quantities wey change together (Grade 3–4 level)
y-m-11-03.title: Finding and correcting rule from bike rental price table
y-m-11-03.topic: Testing rule whenever information increase, and fixing range when new condition (maximum price) appear
y-m-11-03.goal: Test rule wey you make from few table cells against new cell, and when new condition show on sign, fix range where rule correct and make several cases.
y-m-11-03.material: You wan know prices at bike rental shop for park. Price depend on rental time, and dem only rent in 1-hour units, exactly 1 hour, 2 hours, 3 hours, and so on. I go give you information one piece at a time.
y-m-11-03.thinking.0: Guessing from small data and adjusting how sure you be
y-m-11-03.thinking.1: Changing or keeping your judgment according to new information
y-m-11-03.thinking.2: Making several answers under one condition
y-m-11-03.prereq.1: Calculating money in units of one thousand 원
y-m-11-03.s.s1.prompt: Each time one piece of information increase, choose answer wey fit.
y-m-11-03.s.s1.hint.0: Write numbers of cells dem tell you about at each step side by side in table.
y-m-11-03.s.s1.hint.1: Distinguish whether new information 'confirm di rule' or 'change range of di rule'.
y-m-11-03.s.s1.st.0.info: If you rent for 1 hour, price na 3000원, and if 2 hours, na 4000원.
y-m-11-03.s.s1.st.0.ask: How much price go be if you rent for 3 hours?
y-m-11-03.s.s1.st.0.after: Price go up by 1000원 between two cells, so you fit guess 3 hours go cost 5000원. But only two data cells dey, so e no certain.

y-m-11-04.title: Cutting out 3×3 block from calendar
y-m-11-04.topic: Finding relationship between numbers wey be neighbors across and down in calendar number pattern
y-m-11-04.goal: Make your own examples to check say sum of 3×3 block for calendar look like multiple of middle number, and explain with pairing why e hold even if number of cells in row change.
y-m-11-04.material:
Dis na calendar for month with 31 days. 1st na Sunday, and 7 cells dey in one row (Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat). First row na 1~7, second 8~14, third 15~21, fourth 22~28, fifth 29, 30, 31. If you go one cell right, number increase by 1; if you go one cell down, number increase by 7.
Harin cut square shape (9 cells) from calendar, 3 cells across and 3 down, add all 9 numbers and talk, "E look like multiple of middle cell number!"
y-m-11-04.thinking.0: Checking observation by making your own examples
y-m-11-04.thinking.1: Looking at condition wey make relationship hold (cells fit inside calendar)
y-m-11-04.thinking.2: Explaining why e happen (reason for rule)
y-m-11-04.prereq.0: Looking at how numbers change one cell right and one cell down in number pattern (Grade 3–4 level)
y-m-11-04.s.s1.prompt: Make examples to check Harin observation. Choose middle cell number m so all 9 cells fit as connected square in calendar, and write sum s of all 9 numbers. Make 3 examples with different middle numbers.
y-m-11-04.s.s1.hint.0: Choose one middle cell in calendar and first write three cells each for upper, middle, and lower rows.
y-m-11-04.s.s1.hint.1: Write di sum wey you find next to middle number and compare relationship between both.

y-m-11-04.s.s1.fail.c1: Rows above and below middle cell must both dey in calendar. Choose middle number again.
y-m-11-04.s.s1.ok.c2: Di 9 cells connect as cells in same rows.
y-m-11-04.s.s1.fail.c2: If middle cell na Saturday or Sunday, cell to right (or left) go enter next (or previous) row. Change weekday of middle cell.
y-m-11-04.s.s1.fail.c3: Sum of 9 cells different from numbers in calendar. Check again di 8 cells around middle one.
y-m-11-04.s.s1.explain: For example, if middle na 10, sum of 9 cells na 90; for 13 na 117; and for 18 na 162. For all three examples, sum na 9 times middle number. If middle cell na Saturday or Sunday, di 9 cells no connect as square.

y-m-11-04.s.s2.r.a: You think rule dey because of number 7. For 5-cell calendar, write by yourself how much cells above and below bigger or smaller than middle.
y-m-11-04.s.s2.o.b: You need know number of cells in one row to decide how many times middle number sum be
y-m-11-04.s.s2.r.b: You think e depend on number of cells. Set row cell number to 5 and write cells above and below to check wetin happen.
y-m-11-04.s.s2.o.c: Even if one row get 5 cells, sum na 9 times middle number.
y-m-11-04.s.s2.r.c: Dis judgment think relationship between cells above and below fit be similar even if number of cells change.
y-m-11-04.s.s2.o.d: If one row get 5 cells, e go be 5 times middle number.
y-m-11-04.s.s2.r.d: You think number of cells per row multiply straight into sum. Add 9 numbers yourself for 5-cell calendar to check.
y-m-11-04.s.s2.explain: No matter how many cells in a row, with middle cell as reference, cells above and below make one pair, one smaller and one bigger by same amount; left and right cells too make one pair. Sum of each pair na 2 times middle number, so 4 pairs and middle cell make 9 times middle number.
y-m-11-04.s.s3.prompt: Harin wonder why. When middle number na m, pair cells two at a time or group dem one row at a time, then explain why sum of 9 cells na multiple of middle number.
y-m-11-04.s.s3.hint.0: Compare sum of two cells on opposite sides of middle cell with middle number.

y-m-11-04.s.s3.model.0: With middle number m, cell above, m-7, plus cell below, m+7, na 2m. Left m-1 and right m+1 na 2m too, and both diagonal pairs na 2m too. 4 pairs make 8m, then add middle m to get 9m, dat is 9 times middle number.

y-m-11-05.title: If one side double, di other side double too?
y-m-11-05.topic: Comparing how other quantity change when one of two quantities wey change together double
y-m-11-05.goal: From four tables, choose cases where other side exactly double when one side double, and explain with counterexample why being right for two cases no mean e correct for all cases.
y-m-11-05.material:
Mina talk, “When two things change together, if one side double, di other side surely double too!” You wan check by looking at tables for four situations. (All values follow one fixed rule.)
- Pencils: 1 pencil 500원, 2 pencils 1000원, 4 pencils 2000원
- Delivery: 1kg 3000원, 2kg 4000원, 4kg 6000원
- Area of square: side 1cm, 1cm²; side 2cm, 4cm²; side 4cm, 16cm² (read as square centimeters)
- Perimeter of square: side 1cm, 4cm; side 2cm, 8cm; side 4cm, 16cm
y-m-11-05.thinking.1: Finding gap in reasoning wey generalize from two cases
y-m-11-05.prereq.0: Reading how two quantities change together in table (Grade 3–4 level)
y-m-11-05.s.s1.prompt: For each table, first number double from 1 to 2 and 2 to 4. Choose all situations where second number too become exactly 2 times both times.

y-m-11-05.s.s1.hint.1: Check second cell to third cell the same way, and keep only tables wey be 2 times both times.
y-m-11-05.s.s1.r.a: Dis choice check cell by cell whether perimeter become 2 times both times when side double.
y-m-11-05.s.s1.r.b: Check how many times 3000원 become from first cell to second.
y-m-11-05.s.s1.r.c: One cell get area 4 times bigger. Write how many times e become for every cell.
y-m-11-05.s.s1.r.d: Dis choice check say because each pencil cost same, if number of pencils double, price too double.
y-m-11-05.s.s1.explain: Pencils cost 500원, 1000원, 2000원, so na 2 times both times; perimeter na 4, 8, 16, 2 times each time too. Delivery go from 3000 to 4000, wey no be 2 times, and area go from 1 to 4, wey na 4 times.
